name: Paper Before Render
purpose: Separate spatial comprehension from image synthesis so a partly correct internal model cannot silently become an incorrect rendered object.
principle: Think in linked projections and slices first. Render only after the paper model is sufficiently coherent and a human explicitly launches the render stage.

definitions.enough: All hard invariants and major-form relations are mutually consistent; remaining uncertainty is non-gating and explicitly listed. Enough is not maximal detail.
definitions.paper: A non-rendered object state expressed through authority references, topology, dimensions, coordinate frames, linked projections, ordered slices, feature correspondence and unresolved items.
definitions.render: A downstream visual experiment or deliverable. It is evidence of projection behavior, never a replacement authority for the object.

requirements: Identify the richest available object authority and environment authority separately.
Freeze protected surroundings when the task is an object-only edit.
List hard invariants, allowed changes and forbidden changes.
Do not promote a generated image, diagram or projection above its source authority.
Preserve object identity and topology before appearance.
Define one local object frame and keep it fixed across every view.
Record major dimensions, proportions and attachment/host relations.
Use enough non-parallel projections to constrain the major form.
Use ordered sections or slices where depth is ambiguous.
Assign correspondence identities to the same features across views and slices.
Keep object state separate from observer state: camera, projection, crop, viewpoint and wording.
Declare for every lossy abstraction: preserves, discards and safeFor.
Maintain an explicit unresolved list instead of guessing.

passWhen: All hard invariants are satisfied simultaneously.
Major form, orientation, depth, center/attachment and topology agree across the selected projections/slices.
No projection requires rotating, deforming or simplifying the object to make the view fit.
Every remaining uncertainty is non-gating for major form and placement.
The paper state is sufficient to explain expected occlusion and perspective without changing object identity.
states.failAction: Return to P1_PAPER_OBJECT. Do not render.
states.passAction: Set paperReady=true and stop. Ask the human for explicit launch authorization before rendering.

requirements: Present the paper-ready summary and unresolved non-gating details.
Ask the human whether to launch rendering.
No render call occurs without explicit launch authorization.
Render from the paper-ready object state; do not derive new geometry from the target image silhouette.
For bounded image edits, preserve pixels outside the authorized edit region whenever the tool permits.
Observer/camera changes may alter projection and visibility but may not mutate the object state.
Do not count visible subcomponents as geometry authority; visibility is an outcome of projection and occlusion.
Treat the render as a candidate observation, not as the new object authority.
Compare the candidate to frozen authorities and the paper-ready invariants.
Judge major form before small artifacts.
If any hard invariant or major-form relation fails, reject the candidate and return to P1 or P4 as appropriate.
Never average a failed final result with partially correct reasoning: task validity is gated by simultaneous hard invariants.

launchContract.assistantPrompt: Paper stage is ready enough. Launch the rendering stage?
